newsitem.title: YEMEN: Son of Yemen minister shot dead in tribal feud.
newsitem.headline: Son of Yemen minister shot dead in tribal feud.

text.p: A son of Yemen's transport minister was killed in the Yemeni capital Sanaa in a shooting linked to a tribal feud, a security official said on Friday.
The official said Mohammad Ahmad Hussein, 27, was killed on Thursday after gunmen opened fire on his car in central Sanaa. A relative, who was a passenger in the car, was injured.
The victim was a son of Transport Minister Ahmad Musaed Hussein, who belongs to Yemen's ruling party, the General People's Congress.
The shooting was "an act of retaliation" in a feud between the tribe to which the Hussein family belonged and another tribe, the official said. He did not give further details.

Impoverished Yemen, where many people carry weapons, has been plagued by violence. At least 22 people were killed during and after general elections last month. Officials said the incidents were linked to family or tribal disputes, not politics.
Tribesmen with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have seized foreign tourists and diplomats to use as bargaining chips. All hostages have been released unharmed.
